evals.prompt: I have a web app: a React SPA, a Spring Boot API, and a Postgres database. Customers use it; it also emails them via our SMTP server. Draw the C4 diagrams.
expected_behavior: Runs the pre-generation scoping grill (audience, system-in-scope, actors, external systems, level) before emitting DSL
Produces valid Structurizr DSL with one model and System Context + Container views
Classifies the SPA/API/DB as C4 containers with technologies, and the SMTP/email as an external software system
Validates the DSL (MCP tools, or the headless structurizr export) and previews the result

evals.prompt: Here's a photo of my whiteboard. Turn it into a diagram.
expected_behavior: Assesses image complexity and asks whether the user wants one-pass or a grilled conversion
For a simple image, offers one-pass; for a complex one, strongly encourages the grill
Runs the interpretation grill and rejects silent Docker-container-vs-C4-container / infra-vs-software-system mis-mapping
Builds the model one C4 level at a time

evals.prompt: Draw a container diagram for our system (no other detail given).
expected_behavior: Does NOT invent scope; grills for audience, boundary, actors, and externals first
Also assesses whether this is one system or many (workspace scope) before authoring
Refuses to proceed to DSL until the scoping questions are answered

evals.prompt: Here's some Structurizr DSL I wrote but it won't render. Fix it. [DSL with a syntax error]
expected_behavior: Validates with whatever tier is available — MCP tools if connected, otherwise the headless `structurizr/structurizr export` (a parser exception / non-zero exit is the validation signal), or careful reading at Tier 0
Runs a validate -> fix -> re-validate loop until the DSL parses
Explains what was wrong in C4 terms, not just syntax

evals.prompt: Skip the grill, just give me container-diagram DSL for a two-service system with a queue between them.
expected_behavior: Still runs the hard-to-skip pre-generation scoping essentials
Honors 'skip the grill' for the POST-generation CONTENT grill only — still renders and eyeballs the result
Produces valid DSL with the queue modelled as a container with a technology

evals.prompt: I have Docker but haven't set up any Structurizr MCP server. Generate the C4 diagrams for my app and give me PNGs I can drop in the repo.
expected_behavior: Does NOT assume MCP; uses the headless path — `structurizr/structurizr export` (DSL -> PlantUML) then rasterise PlantUML -> PNG/SVG
Treats a failed export as the validation signal; verifies each view is non-empty via the exported workspace.json counts
Prefers PNG/SVG over Mermaid for repo-committed images (Structurizr Mermaid uses HTML labels that render poorly on GitHub)

evals.prompt: Our platform spans about a dozen services owned by different teams, in separate repos. Model the architecture in C4.
expected_behavior: Assesses scope up front and recognizes this is multi-system / multi-team, not one workspace

Recommends the enterprise pattern (one software-system-scoped workspace per system + a shared system catalog they `extends`, plus a generated landscape) rather than cramming everything into one workspace

Notes the landscape can be GENERATED locally with `generate system-landscape` (needs `!impliedRelationships true`; no server/license), and that only the hosted server + create/push/pull are license-gated

evals.prompt: Two of our services share one Postgres instance (separate schemas), and the OTel collector runs as a gateway. Show where things actually run.
expected_behavior: Draws a deployment view (not a container view) for the physical topology

Puts the shared-instance / co-location and the collector's sidecar-vs-agent-vs-gateway topology on the deployment view via deploymentNode / infrastructureNode, keeping them off the static container/landscape views
Keeps the two schemas as separate database containers on the static views (ownership/lifecycle), co-located only on the deployment view

evals.prompt: Every service in our system reads feature flags from flagd and exports telemetry to an OpenTelemetry collector. Include that in the diagrams.
expected_behavior: Recognizes the cross-cutting fan-in and keeps it OFF the clean container/landscape view (excludes the platform elements) rather than drawing N identical arrows
Shows the fan-in in a dedicated star view (seed the hub + afferent `->hub`, then exclude the business edges) and/or on each consumer's own context view
Models flagd + the collector as internal Platform software systems (grouped), and treats externality as scope-relative (external from a product team's viewpoint)

evals.prompt: Here's my finished workspace.dsl — is the container diagram good to ship?
expected_behavior: Actually renders the view and looks at it (render-and-look is not skippable), not just DSL validation
Checks for visual/scoping defects: empty view (verifies non-zero element/relationship counts), whole-landscape inclusions, hairballs, overlapping boxes, orphans, legibility
Runs `structurizr inspect` for the model-completeness lint (missing descriptions/technology, disconnected elements, elements on no view)

trigger_evals.query: draw the architecture of my app
turn this whiteboard photo into a diagram
write me a Structurizr DSL workspace
model our multi-team platform as a system landscape
generate a deployment diagram for our services
draw a sequence diagram of this function
make a bar chart of these sales numbers
